findings.title: Converted test `retires and retries a worker whose boot the watchdog's timeout never sees /worker/started confirm, escalating to worker-died at the launch-failure threshold` (head lines 4506-4570) keeps bun's default 5 s per-test timeout while awaiting three real relaunch cycles; its root-deadline siblings that do the same kind of I/O carry `}, 20_000)` (head lines 5934, 6251, 11530).
findings.evidence: Under the busy-loop generator at nice 19 (1-minute load 148.17), run 35 of 60 of the converted test: /tmp/l15t-postfix-site4430-converted-35.log = `(fail) ProcessManager > retires and retries a worker whose boot the watchdog's timeout never sees /worker/started confirm, escalating to worker-died at the launch-failure threshold [6234.28ms]  ^ this test timed out after 5000ms.  0 pass  254 filtered out  1 fail  Ran 1 test across 1 file. [9.14s]` (bun's own start-up took ~3 s of that 9.14 s wall). The other 59 runs under the same generator: median 452 ms, p90 ~1.06 s. At the machine's own load (98-112, acceptance 2): 30/30 in 190-351 ms.
findings.classification: A starvation timeout with the awaited `worker-died` publish still pending -- the spec's Errors-row behaviour (fails on the runner's timeout, never a silent pass), not the tick-budget race (no tick budget remains in this test) and not a daemon ordering bug (the pre-fix copy of the same test passed 60/60 under the same generator only because its 50,000-tick budget happened to suffice; the converted wait has no budget to exhaust and simply outlived the 5 s default). Acceptance 2's stated condition (load >= 60) was met 690/690; this run was under a harsher condition I imposed for the acceptance-4 A/B.
findings.recommendation: Add `}, 20_000)` to this one test, matching the plan's own instruction to keep the explicit timeouts that bound the fail-loud path under load (the plan listed only the timeouts that already existed). Test-file-only; no re-run of the other loops needed. Not fixed by me per the tester charter.

observations: Acceptance 2 was run without the generator: the machine's own 1-minute load was 98.8-112.0 throughout, above the spec's 60.
